To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the clinical placement process is complex, with many variables that affect the experience of nursing students and their preceptors.

nursing students are perceived to be a valuable resource for the future of the profession of nursing and that the nursing faculty and hospital personnel must collaborate to ensure the success of the clinical placement experience.

the clinical placement of nursing education issues associated are complex and varied and that a lack of communication and consistency in terminology and roles are major issues that need to be addressed in order to provide quality clinical placement experiences for nursing students.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perceptions of hospital personnel associated with student clinical placements.
the need for nursing education to address the issues related to student clinical placement and to work collaboratively with clinical partners.
the need to improve the clinical learning experience of nursing students and to provide a framework for the development of a model to facilitate the process of student clinical placement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the participants in this study perceived the current clinical placements of nursing students as being inadequate.

the clinical placement of nursing student experiences are perceived by hospital personnel as a valuable resource for the future nursing workforce and that the process could be more efficient and effective if there were consistent definitions of student and preceptors roles, a more consistent terminology, and more consistent processes for placement.
the nursing shortage has created a need for more nursing students and clinical placements, which in turn has placed a strain on hospital resources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need for a national standardization of the clinical placement process.
nursing education issues related to student clinical placement are not being adequately addressed by the schools.
nursing students are an important asset to the nursing profession and the health care system, yet the current system for clinical placement of students in hospitals is flawed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical education of students is a partnership that requires the input of all involved.
there is no standardization of clinical education.
there are a multitude of factors that affect the ability of nursing students to have a quality clinical experience.
